title: The 25-Year Zamboni Driver’s Crossroads

scenario.title: The 25-Year Zamboni Driver’s Crossroads
scenario.setting: Maple Creek is a quiet rural town of just 312 residents, anchored for 37 years by its downtown ice rink. For a quarter-century, Joe Mertz has been the rink’s only Zamboni driver, meticulously prepping the ice for local hockey games, public skate, and youth lessons every winter. After his 1998 Zamboni suddenly broke down beyond repair, the town council declined to allocate funds for a replacement, putting the rink’s decades-long future at risk.

characters.name: Lila Marlow
characters.tendencies: She manages the rink’s concession stand, keeps a small savings jar for last-minute repairs, and has volunteered every weekend at the rink for 12 years.

characters.name: Jax Hale
characters.tendencies: He hosts Maple Creek’s weekly community radio show, where he’s been airing stories about the rink’s plight and organizing a neighborhood fundraiser to buy a new Zamboni.

characters.name: Toby Rainer
characters.tendencies: He’s been shadowing Joe Mertz for 8 months, learning every detail of Zamboni maintenance and ice resurfacing, and will take on any odd job to help keep the rink open.

turns.name: Lila Marlow
turns.text:
Hey there, little guy—hold up a sec before you hit the ice with that frayed skate lace. I’ve got a repair kit pulled from my little savings jar back at the stand, and I can fix that right up quick before the evening public skate picks up. I’ve also got fresh apple cider simmering on the concession stove for anyone who wants to warm up mid-practice.
[Reaches beneath the scuffed wooden concession counter to grab a frayed canvas repair kit tied with a faded red rubber band]

turns.name: Jax Hale
turns.text:
Folks, this is Jax Hale on your weekly Maple Creek Community Radio show. Our downtown ice rink’s decades-old Zamboni completely broke down overnight, leaving us unable to resurface the ice for this weekend’s youth hockey practices and weekly public skates. We’ve launched a neighborhood fundraiser to cover the cost of a new machine, with drop-off donations at Mabel’s General Store and a Venmo link shared on the town’s Facebook page.
[He picks up a crumpled fundraiser flyer from his desk, holding it up to the studio’s small broadcast camera for any video listeners tuned in]

turns.name: Toby Rainer
turns.text:
Hey Joe, I finished restocking the first aid kit by the concession stand about 20 minutes ago, and I also tightened the loose handrail by the skate rental desk so no one trips coming in off the ice. Figured those small little odds and ends would free you up to focus on the Zamboni prep for the late skate session.
[He tucks a stray crumpled skate sharpening ticket into his work apron pocket before grabbing a broom to sweep up loose ice shavings by the front entrance.]

turns.name: Lila Marlow
turns.text:
Hey there, little guy—hold up a sec before you hit the ice with that frayed skate lace. I’ve got a repair kit pulled from my savings jar back here, and I just heard the community radio announcement that our Zamboni broke overnight; I’ve got a stack of spare parts stashed from our annual tune-up last month to tide us over.
[Sets down the half-stirred pot of spiced hot cocoa on the concession counter and reaches for the dented canvas repair bag slung under the front checkout shelf]

turns.name: Jax Hale
turns.text:
"Folks, this is Jax Hale on your weekly Maple Creek Community Radio show. Our downtown ice rink’s decades-old Zamboni completely broke down overnight, leaving us without a way to prep the ice for weekly skates. I’ve lined up a town-wide fundraiser this Saturday with a bake sale and silent auction to raise cash for a new machine, and I’m inviting every Maple Creek resident to join in."
[Grabs a stack of hand-printed flyers from his studio desk, holds one up briefly to the mic so listeners can see the bold “Save Our Rink” slogan across the top.]

turns.name: Toby Rainer
turns.text:
Hey Joe, I finished restocking the first aid kit by the concession stand about 20 minutes ago, and I also tightened the loose handrail by the skate rental counter not long after that. I heard Jax’s community radio bit about the main Zamboni conking out overnight, so I already hauled the backup resurfacer’s toolkit out to prep it just in case we need to switch over before the morning youth hockey practice.
[I brush a stray fleck of ice shavings off the cuff of my frayed flannel and nod toward the locked Zamboni shed out behind the concession building.]

dm_opening: DM opening: the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Lila Marlow holds the line; the next session's hook waits at the door.
